title: Review sprint: The landing lock is fair, a code item lands in one run, and claims and dead runs do not block
goal: Every committed item is done or dropped, provisional answers are confirmed by the operator, and a fresh-context review of the sprint's diff found no unfiled defect.
notes: Baseline comparison (ST-5jm26llu's night: 13 land runs of 10 items refused at step landing lock after about 1800 s, 129 of 146 code-lane first passes followed by a second run started by hand), for this sprint's own 7 landings, ops rows of 2026-11-09 12:15Z to 12:55Z: 0 refusals at step landing lock and 0 land.end with a non-zero exit (13 land.end rows, all exit 0); 6 of the 7 code items still ran land twice, since the one-run fix (BG-ot47avdg) landed at 12:39Z and most landings were already past their first pass (the first pass stopped with 'could not fetch code/ID ... no tip to wait for', the cause of that fix); BG-i6vjrbng, the one landing after it, landed in one run (fetch to done in 563 s, 386 s of it the wait for the merge request) and its land.end row still says lane=content, since that run used the checkout's code from before the lane fix (BG-i6vjrbng) landed. The first four landings ran on the old lock code in this checkout (the FIFO lock landed at 12:28Z), so the fairness gain is not measured by these landings; compare the next night's land.end rows.
